UberScene 0.6 makes a video file shorter and plainer to write, opens the export to footage Chrome can't read, and
splits the kit so tools and video files each import only what they need.

It has breaking changes. Most files move with one command:

```sh
npx uberscene lint --fix video.tsx
```

## Highlights

- **Everything about an element is a prop.** A value is a constant, or a list of `{ at, value, easing? }` keys when
  it changes. Effects are an `effects` list, a speed ramp is keys on `speed`, and held frames are `freezes`.
  `<Keyframe>`, `<Effect>`, `<SpeedKey>`, `<Freeze>` and `automation` are gone.

  ```tsx
  <Clip id="pour" src="asset:coffee" in={8} out={14}
    transform={{ scale: [{ at: 0, value: 1, easing: "easeInOut" }, { at: 3.5, value: 1.2 }] }}
    effects={[{ type: "lut", src: "asset:warm" }]}
    speed={[{ at: 0, value: 1 }, { at: 1.6, value: 0.4 }]} />
  ```

- **Clips straight in the composition.** A cut needs no `<Track>`. Clips written in `<Composition>` play in order as
  the main track, and tracks written beside them draw on top.

  ```tsx
  <Composition width={1920} height={1080} fps={30}>
    <Clip id="opening" src="asset:intro" />
    <Clip id="interview" src="asset:talk" in={2} out={12} />
  </Composition>
  ```

- **Native codecs (experimental).** With `UBERSCENE_CODECS`, UberScene decodes and encodes with its own Rust codecs
  (FilmCraft's craft-video and craft-audio, no FFmpeg). They read HEVC, ProRes and DNxHR, which Chrome can't without
  a GPU, and write H.264, ProRes masters in `.mov` (`--codec prores`) and the soundtrack. The first native export
  downloads them for your machine from this release; `npx uberscene codecs install` fetches them ahead.
- **A `recolor` effect.** It turns one colour into another and leaves the rest of the picture:
  `effects={[{ type: "recolor", from: "#c4202b", to: "#2f9e4f" }]}`.
- **Blocks.** Nine scene-sized pieces of motion design ship with the CLI: ranked lists, bar races, chat reveals,
  terminal typing and more. `uberscene blocks` lists them, and `uberscene blocks add` drops one into a file.
- **The editor.** `@uberscene/editor` gives editor parts that share one player (preview, layers, timeline). A shadcn
  editor builds on them: `npx shadcn add https://uberscene.prefixtree.xyz/r/editor.json`.
- **`uberscene lint`** runs the checks from the command line, and `--fix` applies their fixes, the 0.6 renames
  included.

## Breaking changes

`uberscene lint --fix` moves each of these, except where noted.

- **Props, not children:** keys, `effects`, `speed`, `freezes`, and `volume` and `pan` keys replace the removed
  elements and `automation`.
- **One name for one idea.**
  - A kind is always `type`: a shape's `shape`, a title's `animation.preset`, a lower third's `variant`,
    `background.mode`, an SVG's `color.mode`.
  - A line's width is `thickness`.
  - A shadow's `radius` is `blur`.
  - The zoom transition's `blur` is `smear`, and the scanlines effect's `thickness` is `coverage`.
  - Values are camelCase (`easeInOut`).
- **One way to style text:** a title's look is one `style` (a preset name, or an object of `font`, `size`, `color`
  and the rest), not thirteen flat props.
- **One coordinate system:** every element that draws is placed by `box`, in pixels from the top left.
- **Props that were never drawn are errors:** `fit` on titles, shapes and stickers; `blendOpacity` outside clips;
  `transform` on `<Adjustment>`. Delete them; the picture doesn't change. Not moved by `--fix`.
- **Removed components:** `Frame`, `Background`, `ProgressBar`, `Arrow`, `Highlight` and `QuoteCard`. Draw them as a
  `<Shape>`, a background or free code; a quote is the `quote-build` block. Not moved by `--fix`.
- **Time in ticks:** frame and sample maths are exact, `FRAME_EPS` is gone, and `fps` takes NTSC rates such as
  `"29.97"`.
- **The kit is split:** `@uberscene/kit` keeps what a video file imports. Tools import from the new `@uberscene/sdk`
  (resolver, actions, executor, write-back) and `@uberscene/kit/schema` (the vocabulary as data). Video files need no
  change.
- **Chrome 157 only:** the export refuses any other Chrome named by `UBERSCENE_CHROMIUM`.

## Packages

- New: `@uberscene/sdk` and `@uberscene/editor`.
- All packages share the version 0.6.0. Each package's `CHANGELOG.md` lists every change.

## Fixes

- **Security:**
  - An SVG from someone else can no longer run script: its cleaning now ignores case and namespaces.
  - An asset id can no longer reach a file outside the media folder through the export's local server.
- **Export:**
  - A failed export keeps the file it would have replaced.
  - A missing asset stops the export at once, and a cancel stops it straight away.
  - Long exports no longer run out of memory.
  - A frame that fails to decode is reported instead of repeating the last one.
- **Player:**
  - Reverse playback decodes every frame.
  - WebGL contexts, shaders and audio contexts are released.
  - A box with keys keeps its size.
  - Timecode is right at rates such as 12.5 fps.
- **Editing:**
  - Removing, splitting and trimming a clip carry what is anchored to it.
  - Undo then save writes an element once.
  - Saves no longer fail after a track is deleted.
  - An edit that would break the file is refused (`BREAKS_FILE`).
- **Other:**
  - `narrate()` times text in any script.
  - Long anchor chains are no longer reported as cycles.
  - `uberscene skills install --force` deletes nothing it didn't write.

## Upgrade

```sh
npm install uberscene@0.6.0 @uberscene/kit@0.6.0
npx uberscene lint --fix src/**/*.tsx
```

Tools built on the kit's resolver or actions add `@uberscene/sdk` and move those imports to it.
